newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-OLYMPIC CHAMPIONS RETURN TO ATLANTA INDOOR MEET.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-OLYMPIC CHAMPIONS RETURN TO ATLANTA INDOOR MEET.

text.p: - About 10 Olympic gold medalists return to the city of their 1996 triumphs this weekend for the USA Indoor championships, the final tuneup before next week's World Indoor Track and Field Championships.

This year's U.S. indoor championships are restricted to Americans for the first time. Many of the athletes here are looking ahead one week to the world championships in Paris, where for the first time money will be at stake for the top finishers.
This weekend's meet will decide most of the U.S. entrants for the worlds.

The most important non-contestant for this year's meet in Atlanta is Michael Johnson, double Olympic gold medalist in the 200 and 400 meters. Johnson will work as an analyst on the American telecast of the meet.

Among the headliners in Atlanta are: Gail Devers, gold medalist in the 100 meters and 4x100 relay; Allen Johnson, gold medalist in he 110-meter hurdles; Charles Austin, Olympic high jump champion; Kenny Harrison, triple jump gold medalist; and Randy Barnes, shot put winner.

Other well-known entrants this weekend include 100-meter runner Dennis Mitchell, the U.S. Olympic team captain; ageless distance runner Mary Slaney, and Atlanta hometown favourite Gwen Torrence, bronze medalist in the Olympic 100 meters and a part of the gold medal American 4x100 relay team.

At the World's in Paris, the first three places in each event in Paris will claim $50,000, $20,000 and $10,000, respectively, in prize money. Winning relay teams will split $60,000, $20,000 and $10,000 for first, second and third.
